description: Young innovators combining code, creativity, and science to build smarter health tech for safer space missions.
summary:
**PRANREKHA: Every Signal Matters** is an interactive astronaut health-monitoring software prototype developed by Team PRANREKHA for NASA Space Apps Challenge 2026, addressing the challenge of creating health-monitoring software for astronauts on space missions.

Prolonged exposure to microgravity can affect cardiovascular function, bone density, muscle strength, fluid distribution, sleep and overall wellbeing. Monitoring these changes is essential for supporting astronaut health during long-duration missions.

PRANREKHA provides an integrated platform where users can select astronaut profiles and missions, record vital signs such as heart rate, oxygen saturation, blood pressure, body temperature and respiratory rate, and monitor sleep and fatigue. Its Microgravity Impact Explorer explains six key dimensions of spaceflight health. The platform also includes optional menstrual-health tracking, mission timelines, indicative health flags and reporting features.

Built using HTML, CSS and JavaScript, the current prototype stores records locally in the browser and visualises submitted data. It demonstrates how astronaut health information can be organised and reviewed in one interface.

Future development could include secure cloud storage, validated anomaly-detection systems, real-time spacesuit sensor integration and individualised health monitoring.

PRANREKHA aims to make astronaut health data more accessible, organised and meaningful, because every signal matters.
details:
PRANREKHA: Every Signal Matters is an interactive astronaut health-monitoring software prototype developed by Team PRANREKHA for NASA Space Apps Challenge 2026.

Prolonged exposure to microgravity can affect cardiovascular function, bone density, muscle strength, fluid distribution, sleep and overall wellbeing. PRANREKHA addresses the need to organise and interpret astronaut health information through a unified, mission-oriented platform.

Users can select individual astronaut profiles and missions, record physiological measurements such as heart rate, oxygen saturation, blood pressure, body temperature and respiratory rate, and monitor sleep and fatigue. The Mission Control Dashboard presents these indicators visually, while indicative health flags highlight readings that may require further attention. The Microgravity Impact Explorer explains six dimensions of spaceflight-related health changes. Additional features include optional menstrual-health tracking, mission timelines, health summaries and data export.

The project aims to make astronaut health information more organised, accessible and easier to review, supporting informed monitoring during long-duration missions. Its intended impact is to contribute towards more individualised astronaut healthcare and encourage attention to physiological changes throughout space exploration.

We developed the prototype using HTML5, CSS3 and JavaScript, with browser Local Storage for data persistence and Netlify for public hosting. The platform currently operates as a front-end prototype using illustrative records; it does not yet connect to real-time spacecraft sensors or provide clinical diagnoses.

Our creative approach lies in integrating multiple dimensions of astronaut health into one interactive interface rather than treating each measurement independently. We also included menstrual-health tracking to recognise individual physiological needs that are often overlooked in generalised monitoring concepts.

During development, we considered usability, clarity of medical information, mission-specific organisation, individual differences, data accessibility, privacy limitations and the technical feasibility of future sensor integration.

PRANREKHA's central belief is simple: every mission matters, but every astronaut matters just as much.
